$comment: Provider error corpus for the quota classifier (intent-hq/intent#7615).
Every entry is an error the pinned ACP adapters actually send to intentd, taken from the pinned packages, not hand-written.
`kinds` lists every structured error kind each pinned adapter can attach. tests/provider_error_corpus.rs renders each kind and checks the classifier.

scripts/check-provider-error-corpus.py downloads the pinned adapters and fails when they emit a kind missing here, when a listed kind disappears, when the adapter's own category disagrees with `expect`, or when a Claude Agent SDK usage-limit prefix has no rendering below. CI runs it on every PR, so an adapter pin bump that adds a limit wording fails before it merges.

`expect` is what intentd should do: `quota` means backup failover and the quota banner fire. `knownGap` marks an entry the classifier gets wrong today, and `textOnlyKnownGap` a Claude rendering it only catches through its errorKind (claude-agent-acp can send the same text with no data); the test asserts each gap still exists, so fixing one means deleting the field.

Renderings follow what intentd sees: intentd does not advertise the sessionFailure capability, so claude-agent-acp keeps the detail in `message` (`Internal error: <detail>`) and codex-acp only raises a JSON-RPC error for usageLimitExceeded (other codex kinds stream as text).

claude-code.$comment: claude-agent-acp attaches {"errorKind": <kind>} as JSON-RPC data. Kinds: the Claude Agent SDK's SDKAssistantMessageError union plus the adapter's own kinds. The adapter's providerFailureCategory maps rate_limit to rate_limited and billing_error / account_on_hold to quota_exhausted.

account_on_hold.knownGap: claude-agent-acp maps account_on_hold to quota_exhausted, but the classifier has no marker for it. Claude Code 2.1.280 only raises it as an OAuth error ("Your account is on hold and can't use Claude Code"), so it is not seen on the prompt path yet.

codex.$comment: codex-acp attaches {"message", "codexErrorInfo"} as JSON-RPC data. String kinds and structured kinds (an object keyed by kind, carrying httpStatusCode) come from STRING_CODEX_ERROR_CATEGORIES and STRUCTURED_CODEX_ERROR_CATEGORIES. codex-acp maps any kind with httpStatusCode 429 to rate_limited, so the test also renders every structured kind with 429 and expects quota. WIRE GAP: that mapping and every kind except those in raisedAsRpcError only exist on codex-acp's typed session-failure path, which intentd does not advertise. Today intentd receives rateLimitExceeded, HTTP 429 and the rest as streamed agent text with no prompt error, so neither failover nor the quota banner can see them; these kind cases pin the classifier for the day they arrive as errors.
